content.overview: Specialist instruction for stock-area biosecurity, quarantine & movement control in donor/mother plant systems.

sections.title: Stock areas deserve separate controls
sections.body: Mother/stock plants can multiply biological risk across many downstream propagules. Clean, incoming, suspect and held material therefore need explicit boundaries.

sections.title: Tools and plant movement are transmission pathways
sections.body: Cutting, pruning and plant-contact workflows can move sap-associated biological hazards; sanitation and movement controls must follow the facility's validated procedures.

sections.title: A quarantine label without operational separation is weak control
sections.body: Status must affect placement, movement, tools, access and release authority rather than existing only as a label.

commonMistakes: Treating visual health as proof of clean-stock status.
content.practicalApplication: Review a donor-management scenario, preserve identity and status evidence, and document the strongest supported next action without overstating cause or cleanliness.
content.summary: Donor management depends on traceable identity, plant-health evidence, controlled movement and longitudinal performance records.
